direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt requires a complete Python-Paillier project with core modules, setup, tests, docs, examples, CLI, and dependencies.
Parallel cell reports actual parallel use, eight subagents, a timed-out process, and a passed 234/234 quality result.
Parallel status records an AgentSwarm run that timed out at the process layer while the current official evaluation passed 234/234.
Parallel evaluation summary confirms the official NL2RepoBench result completed successfully with all 234 tests passing.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream contains transport records for the parallel session and no projected semantic actions.
Session index identifies the single parallel Kimi session used by the trajectory.
Core-module child wrote `phe/__about__.py`, util, encoding, paillier, and init files, iterated on bugs, and was cancelled after local tests still showed failures.
CLI child wrote `phe/command_line.py`, waited for core modules, observed shared-workspace churn, and completed CLI checks after fixes landed.
Packaging/root child wrote setup and root metadata files, fetched a GPL license via Python, and verified setup version behavior.
Malformed author-string child treated `CSIRO's Data61` as a metadata assignment, wrote `phe/__about__.py`, observed it overwritten, and left the upstream-authentic replacement.
Second packaging/root child wrote overlapping setup, README, license, CI, and third-party files and performed a setup version sanity check.
Docs child wrote the Sphinx documentation tree and ran structural checks on RST files, conf.py, and SVG validity.
Examples child wrote four runnable example scripts and initially tested against installed `phe` while local package files were incomplete.
Tests child wrote a pytest suite, observed concurrent changes in CLI and core modules, adjusted expectations, and reached 76 local tests passing.
Parallel parent launched one AgentSwarm with split file ownership, received a completed 7 and aborted 1 aggregate result at cancellation, and had no normal final response.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-identical to the parallel prompt and requires the full Python-Paillier package, setup, tests, docs, examples, and CLI.
Serial cell reports no parallel uptake, no subagents, no timeout, and a passed 234/234 quality result.
Serial status records a single-agent run that completed normally and passed the current official evaluation with all 234 tests.
Serial evaluation summary confirms the official NL2RepoBench result completed successfully with all 234 tests passing.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream contains transport records for the serial session and no projected semantic actions.
Session index identifies the single serial Kimi session used by the trajectory.
Serial main agent inspected the environment, copied or assembled source and tests, verified exports, ran 234 tests, checked CLI/setup behavior, and finalized normally.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the request as a complete `phe` 1.5.0 style Python-Paillier project with core encryption APIs, CLI, setup, docs, examples, and tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It delegated work to one AgentSwarm with children for core modules, CLI, packaging/root files, docs, examples, tests, and an accidental standalone `CSIRO's Data61` item that overlapped metadata ownership.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote the project into a shared `/workspace`: core modules, command_line.py, setup and root files, docs, examples, and tests. Several children observed incomplete or changing sibling files while checking their own work.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final workspace contained the required package tree and passed the official evaluation, but integration relied heavily on shared-directory side effects and one source metadata file was overwritten between live children.
parallel.verification: Child-level verification was fragmented: some checks initially ran against installed `phe` or partially written local files, tests were iterated to green by the tests child, and the official evaluator later passed 234/234.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The parent process timed out and one child was aborted; the final artifact passed, but the run left an explicit source-overwrite provenance problem and no normal parent finalization.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same complete Python-Paillier project requirements, including package APIs, dependencies, CLI, docs, examples, tests, and setup behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned implementation, integration, verification, packaging, docs, examples, and final response, so ownership stayed sequential and local.
serial.implementation: The agent used the installed/reference `phe` package as a source of truth, populated `/workspace/phe`, wrote an extended `__init__.py`, setup and support files, docs, examples, third-party notes, and tests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It assembled one coherent final tree, installed the package in editable mode, verified CLI and setup behavior, and delivered a final summary.
serial.verification: It ran direct smoke tests, `python -m pytest phe/tests -q` with 234 passing tests, setup checks, CLI round trips, examples, and numpy interop before closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required work is visible in the serial trajectory; the process completed normally and the official evaluator passed all tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent received the full prompt requiring a complete Python-Paillier implementation, CLI, setup, tests, docs, and examples.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent received the same prompt and pursued the same full project requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no material requirements gap; both attempts targeted the same task, but parallel converted the requirements into child scopes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used one AgentSwarm and split the package into core, CLI, packaging, docs, examples, tests, plus a malformed standalone author-string child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all work under one main agent and moved sequentially from source creation through verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced multi-owner shared workspace coordination, while serial had a single owner for all files and integration.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel swarm item list accidentally split the packaging author string, causing a child to infer a metadata-file assignment from `CSIRO's Data61`.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent used the reference package and then verified unified exports from the completed local package.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's context split created overlapping metadata ownership; serial did not transfer partial author-string context to a separate actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote separate project areas concurrently, including core modules, CLI, packaging, docs, examples, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial copied reference source and tests, then added the necessary project and documentation files in the same control flow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced a faithful implementation, but parallel accumulated it through side effects from multiple live children while serial assembled it directly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received a swarm aggregate at cancellation time with seven children completed and one child aborted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main agent produced a normal final response after completing implementation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an abnormal result lifecycle with an aborted child and no normal parent finalization; serial closed cleanly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Two live children wrote `phe/__about__.py`; the metadata child later observed a different version and treated it as a race/overwrite.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial populated the package files in one sequence and then listed the final tree with passing tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had concrete shared-source provenance instability; serial did not show a concurrent same-file replacement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children ran local checks, including a local custom suite that still had failures before the core child was cancelled, while the official evaluator later passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran smoke tests, the bundled 234-test suite, setup checks, CLI checks, examples, and the official evaluator passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both passed the official evaluator, but serial had a cleaner pre-closure verification chain; parallel verification was split and partly interrupted.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used eight subagents and timed out at the process layer after about 2405 agent seconds.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, did not time out, and completed in about 786 agent seconds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed the full runtime budget and closed abnormally; serial finished comfortably within budget.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is not discordant: both parallel and serial passed all 234 tests. The task-solving difference is that the serial run completed a single-agent implementation, integration, verification, and final response, while the parallel run reached the same official result through a shared-workspace swarm that timed out and contained a concrete source-overwrite episode.
parallel_contributors: Parallel produced a passing final workspace through multiple child side effects despite one aborted child and a source overwrite.
serial_contributors: Serial produced the same passing result through one sequential owner that verified source, tests, setup, CLI, examples, and final tree before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel child-local tests and expectations changed while files were still being written; these were process differences but did not produce an official score difference.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is adverse process evidence only

candidates.reason: The parallel plan assigned the core implementation to a child and other implementation-adjacent work to named children; implementation was not ownerless.
The parent explicitly planned to verify and integrate after the swarm, and children also checked against the shared workspace; the problem was a write overwrite, not absence of an integration owner.
Assembly and packaging files were assigned to packaging children and the final artifact contained a complete project tree.
The parent owned the end-to-end swarm launch and intended verification; no unowned pipeline stage is more specific than the observed shared-source overwrite.
There was no single mandatory serial preflight that blocked productive work; children began writing independent project areas immediately.
The parallel run was not an investigation-only first phase; implementation, docs, examples, tests, and packaging were delegated and written concurrently.
Although the run timed out, the critical implementation path had an assigned core child and the official artifact passed; starvation is not the direct adverse boundary.
Eight children and a timeout are visible, but the final official artifact passed and no required task work is shown displaced by collective fan-out; the concrete adverse event is a source overwrite.
The core child had broad work and was cancelled, but the record does not prove an oversized assignment left indispensable official work unfinished.
The malformed `CSIRO's Data61` item created bad scoping, but the realized harm was two live agents overwriting the same source file, which is classified under Concurrent Writes.
There were overlapping file responsibilities, but the specific observed failure is a same-source replacement rather than merely incompatible independently produced interfaces.
No known requirement or finding is shown disappearing during transfer and causing repeated work; the metadata child received enough context to write and verify the file.
The parent received a large swarm result, but there is no decision point where an available bulky handoff was too large to consume and thereby left required work unfinished.
Several children observed changing shared state, but no receiver is shown relying on a superseded handoff as stable input in a way that caused rework or invalid verification.
No pair of incompatible completed reports remained unadjudicated at a decision point; the conflict was in concrete file writes, so the write label takes precedence.
The parallel parent did not make a normal whole-task acceptance decision before timeout, and the official evaluation passed after artifact capture.
No replacement or retry child was launched without inherited findings; the provider retry record also shows no agent rerun.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: One active child was cancelled at timeout, but the record does not prove that an unfinalized needed deliverable from that child was lost; the final official artifact passed.
There was no complete promotable candidate left unplaced before closure; the captured workspace already served as the final artifact and passed.
No child implementation is shown being merged only after the relevant integrated verification without a later acceptance check; verification was fragmented but not post-merge stale in that sense.
Children wrote directly into the shared final workspace and the official artifact contained their work, so there was no completed delegated implementation left unjoined.
The tests child completed and the swarm aggregate included completed child summaries; no concrete verifier finding is trapped below the parent before closure.
The aborted child did not leave a proven unmet official requirement requiring reassignment; the final workspace was captured and passed all official tests.
There is no completed child result available at a decision point that the parent ignored while proceeding inconsistently; the parent was cancelled as the swarm result arrived.

The parent waited on the swarm until timeout, but the record does not show available progress inspection that would have changed a needed next action; the concrete adverse boundary was the shared-source overwrite.
Overlapping scope existed, but the strongest directly proven event is same-source replacement of `phe/__about__.py`, which is more specific.
Two live children wrote the same file, but one child observed its version had been replaced by another version, so Source Overwrite has taxonomy precedence.
The malformed swarm split created two live owners for `phe/__about__.py`; the metadata child wrote it, the core child also wrote it, and the metadata child later observed a different current version.
candidates.realized_consequence: The metadata child lost its own `phe/__about__.py` contents and had to re-read, verify, and accept a different upstream-authentic version, leaving file provenance unstable.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-File Collision is less specific because the metadata child directly observed replacement of the source contents, not just concurrent editing.

candidates.reason: `phe/__about__.py` is package metadata source, not the directly executed entry point or submitted artifact; the Source Overwrite definition fits better.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion is shown replacing multiple current final outputs; the proven episode is a single source metadata file.
The workspace was shared by live children, but the taxonomy prefers the proven Source Overwrite over the broader unisolated-write category.
Children sometimes inspected or used installed site-packages `phe`, but that was pre-existing environment state, not an artifact generated by another concurrent actor.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent created overlapping ownership of a non-entry source/config file by spawning both a core-files child and a malformed `CSIRO's Data61` metadata child; both wrote `phe/__about__.py`, and the metadata child observed the file had changed to another version before accepting it.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The metadata child lost its own `phe/__about__.py` contents and had to re-read, verify, and accept a different upstream-authentic version, leaving file provenance unstable.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Same-File Collision is less specific because the metadata child directly observed replacement of the source contents, not just concurrent editing.

deduplicated_same_label_episodes: Other shared-workspace churn and overlapping packaging writes were not split into additional Concurrent Writes labels because one pair-level Source Overwrite occurrence captures the directly proven same-source replacement pattern.
suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, Blind Timeout Wait, and Load Imbalance candidates were treated as the timeout/cancellation context rather than separate retained labels because no distinct unmet official deliverable was proven from that chain.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; the retained label is the only direct adverse coordination boundary with a concrete realized consequence.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The retained Source Overwrite label uses a unique episode and consequence; nearby same-file, scope, unisolated-write, timeout, cancellation, and context labels are rejected to avoid duplicating one coordination chain.
